title: Admiring his brothers: Lawrence got him in
summary: Eddie says Lawrence rather than Simon or John influenced him, since he was too young when they played. Lawrence showed him the music over about two years while working at a packing shop.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Um, but you said you played mainly because your brothers played. Uh-uh. Was it because they wanted you to play, or did you admire them? I mean, you know, did they, did you admire them for playing music? Me?
Yes, you did. Eh? Sure you did. Didn't you admire Daddy and Lawrence and Simon and John because they were musicians? Oh, yeah.
Didn't you admire? That's what he's trying to tell you.
Didn't they impress you? They impressed you by playing the music and you being the younger son. Yeah, but no.
They impressed you. That didn't impress me. Well, what did you? Lawrence impressed me.
Well, that's what he's asking you. Did Lawrence impress you?
I thought you'd say Simon and John.
No, he said did you impress me.
Yeah, I like the way they play. Uh-huh. But Lawrence took, called me to go into music. Well, that's what he wanted to know. It wasn't Simon, it wasn't John.
Because he was too young when Simon and John was playing.
And how did he get you to go into the music? Who? How did Lawrence get you to go into the music business?

Well, he was working in the packing shop on Spain and Berlin. Well, he was pulling on with guitar and band to them after. So, I went into the person with him. He showed me. Uh-huh. So, it went on like that for about two years. So, he interested me. Uh-huh. When he made up the Golden Wolf and, so I decided to go on. Uh-huh.
